title: TICK stage 2: run run_reconciliation_tick on its own thread at a 60 s cadence, serialized with entry dispatch by a journal_sync lock (removes ~28 s from the trader tick)
note: [from TICK-DURATION-115S, docs/research/tick-duration-115s-profile-2026-11-04.md section 6] MEASURED 2026-11-04 tick_cost (37 ticks): order_monitor reconciliation half 28.4 s per tick on the main loop. A plain move off-thread is UNSAFE: the reverse reconciler's default ORPHAN_POSITION_POLICY=adopt acts on first sight, and package->trade row takes up to 7.6 s (audit F8, n=40), so a concurrent pass could adopt a duplicate of a fill the main thread has not journaled. Design: one journal_sync lock held by Coordinator.multi_account_execute (place+journal) and by each reconciliation pass (preserves today's invariant); entries wait <= one pass only when a pass is in flight. Needs a replay/equivalence test over recorded ticks. Sweep cadence must stay bounded (60 s), never stopped (Prime Directive). DETECTOR: tick_cost order_monitor ~0 on-loop and tick mean < 40 s over >= 20 ticks. [input from TICK-DURATION-115S stage-1 observation 2026-11-05] After the faster loop (cycle 159 s -> 59 s) one sqlite "database is locked" burst appeared 02:20:41-02:21:04Z: _sweep_package_close_reason_from_trade, _sweep_unlinked_packages, _sweep_stuck_linked_packages failed once each, then venue_protection_snapshot.record_read (timeout=5.0). All contained, retried next pass. Baseline: 0 in a complete journalctl scan 2026-11-04 21:44-23:22Z (21,226 lines). Cause unestablished. Before adding a third DB-writing thread, measure lock frequency over a longer window and identify the lock holder; the journal_sync lock design should also bound sqlite contention. [lane session_01AFoLuLzq1snbogF2qX97Pi 2026-11-05] MEASURED (diag relay issues #23192/#23193): tick_cost one process from 06:51:30Z, 78 ticks: mean 47414.7 ms, order_monitor 23631.5 ms mean. exit_loop_health: 158 intervals, 1 breach, max 71164.1 ms at 08:01:12Z = max_pass_ms 41989.8 at the same instant. The breach is the EXIT PASS itself, not the main tick: journalctl 08:00:30-08:01:12Z shows each of ~15 packages taking 2-7 s (normal whole pass ~1 s) while the main thread logged 'database is locked' at 08:01:05/08:01:11. So stage 2 alone does NOT fix the exit interval. LOCK FREQUENCY, journalctl 'database is locked', 2026-11-04T00:00Z to 2026-11-05T08:12Z (windows 14:30Z-02:00Z and 02:00Z-now complete, 162,226 + 173,173 lines; 00:00-14:36Z window returncode -15, a lower bound): 59 lines in ~16 bursts (10 s to 2 min each); 55 are signal_audit_logger dual-write failures (a waiter), 4 are the 02:20Z order_monitor burst. Lock HOLDER NOT IDENTIFIED: the read-only relay cannot see sqlite lock owners; ml_decision_shadow and db_integrity are ruled out (no journal write / mode=ro). Fix in PR: reconciliation on its own 60 s thread under a journal_sync RLock held by Coordinator.multi_account_execute and run_pairs_tick, AND exit-thread best-effort telemetry writes (position_telemetry, position_path_history, venue_protection_snapshot) get a 0.25 s busy timeout instead of 5 s. Dry soak scripts/ops/soak_reconcile_offtick.py (40 s foreign hold every 90 s, ~1000 s simulated): pre-change exit writes max interval 70.2 s, 7/30 over 60 s; with the change 34.1 s, 0/33. RE-OPENED 2026-11-06 (lane MECH-FOLLOWUPS-1105, manager 2026-11-06a request): the row's observation FAILED as written. (1) EXIT-EVAL INTERVAL BREACHED alerts in 2026-11-05T10:30Z..2026-11-06T10:30Z: 4 (11-05 16:58:00Z 74.3 s; 11-06 00:02:38Z 115.3 s; 02:35:02Z 61.4 s; 03:59:43Z 79.0 s). Population: the newest-400 alert rows, newest 2026-11-06T13:11Z, 5 breach rows total, none after 03:59:43Z. Attribution (journal evidence): 00:02 = Bybit 10006 in-line sleep(15) in get_ohlcv (fixed by #23580, deployed 03:31Z); 16:58, 02:35, 03:59 = trade_journal.db write-lock bursts (not Stage 2 itself): fixed in two steps, #23690 (reconciliation snapshot writes, deployed 07:03:45Z) and #23710 (exit-pass telemetry batch, deployed ~09:11:36Z). exit_interval_soak (log_file?name=exit_interval_soak&lines=1000, 04:59-13:15Z, over_requirement true = 0 of 1000 rows in every window): pre-#23690 05:00-07:03:45Z n=247 max 59.48 s (06:54:10Z), 2 intervals >45 s; #23690 only 07:03:45-09:11:36Z n=255 max 45.69 s, 1 >45 s; with #23710 09:11:36-13:14Z n=484 max 41.26 s, 0 >45 s. (2) tick_cost, current process started 2026-11-06T12:39:02Z, ticks_measured 36: mean_ms 37123.6, max 86563.9 (13:02:28Z): the observation's 'mean_ms < 30000' FAILS (the design note's '< 40 s' detector passes); order_monitor on-loop mean 0.1 ms (n=36): the reconciliation half IS off the tick (the Stage-2 intent is proven). (3) NEW cost it introduced or exposes: journal_sync.wait mean 10126.9 ms, max 23613.2 ms (n=39) = 29.6% of the tick, journal_sync.hold mean 866.6 ms max 5433.1 ms: entries now wait for a reconciliation pass; this is the open question for the next owner.
